subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: In 1492, Christopher Columbus sailed west from Spain across which ocean?
explanation: Columbus sailed west across the Atlantic Ocean in 1492 and reached islands in the Caribbean.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Which civilization built the city of Machu Picchu high in the Andes Mountains?
explanation: The Inca built Machu Picchu in the Andes Mountains of what is now Peru in the 1400s.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: The Aztec capital, Tenochtitlan, stood where ___ City is today.
explanation: Tenochtitlan was built on an island in a lake. Mexico City, the capital of Mexico, stands on the same site today.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Which tool helped sailors know which direction they were heading?
explanation: A magnetic compass points north, so sailors could tell their direction even when they could not see land or stars.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa during a period of great art and learning in Europe. What is that period called?
explanation: The Renaissance was a period of new art, science and learning in Europe from about the 1300s to the 1500s. Leonardo da Vinci was one of its most famous artists.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Why did European explorers in the 1400s search for sea routes to Asia?
choices: To find the hidden source of the Nile River in Africa
To trade for spices, silk and other valuable goods
correctAnswer: To trade for spices, silk and other valuable goods
explanation: Spices, silk and other Asian goods were very valuable in Europe. A direct sea route would let traders buy them without paying the many merchants along the land routes.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498 by sailing around the southern tip of which continent?
explanation: Vasco da Gama of Portugal sailed around the Cape of Good Hope at the southern tip of Africa and reached India in 1498.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Which of these were achievements of the ancient Maya? Select all that apply.
explanation: The Maya of Mexico and Central America developed a writing system, built stone pyramid-temples and created accurate calendars. They did not have printing presses or steamships.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Use the word bank: Magellan, spices, caravels. Europeans wanted ___ such as pepper and cinnamon from Asia. Portuguese sailors used small, fast ships called ___. An expedition first led by Ferdinand ___ was the first to sail all the way around the world.
explanation: Europeans sought Asian spices, the Portuguese explored in caravels and Magellan's expedition (1519-1522) completed the first voyage around the world, although Magellan himself died on the way.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Which of these is a SECONDARY source about Columbus's first voyage?
choices: A journal Columbus kept during the voyage
A letter Columbus wrote to the king and queen of Spain
A map drawn by a sailor on the voyage
explanation: A secondary source is written later by someone who was not there. A modern history book is a secondary source; the journal, letter and map are primary sources.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, built about 1450, changed Europe mainly by doing what?
choices: Making books faster and cheaper to produce
correctAnswer: Making books faster and cheaper to produce
explanation: Before the press, books were copied by hand. Printing made books cheaper and more common, so ideas spread much faster.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: According to the passage, how did the Aztec grow food in a city surrounded by water?
passage: The Aztec built their capital, Tenochtitlan, on an island in Lake Texcoco. Raised roads called causeways linked the island to the shore. Farmers grew corn, beans and squash on chinampas, small plots of rich soil built up in the shallow lake.
choices: They carried all their food across the causeways from far away
They built up plots of soil called chinampas in the lake
correctAnswer: They built up plots of soil called chinampas in the lake
explanation: The passage says farmers grew crops on chinampas, small plots of rich soil built up in the shallow lake.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Put these events in order from earliest to latest.
orderedItems: Magellan's expedition sails around the world
explanation: Marco Polo traveled to China in the late 1200s, Gutenberg built his press about 1450, Columbus crossed the Atlantic in 1492 and Magellan's expedition circled the world from 1519 to 1522.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: What was one major effect on Native American peoples of contact with Europeans after 1492?
choices: Their populations quickly doubled in just a few years
They were not affected by the newcomers in any way
Diseases such as smallpox killed a great many people
correctAnswer: Diseases such as smallpox killed a great many people
explanation: Native Americans had no immunity to diseases such as smallpox and measles brought from Europe. These diseases killed a very large share of the population.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: How were the Aztec and Inca empires alike?
choices: Both were located high in the Andes Mountains of South America
Both built their capitals on islands in a shallow lake
Both were located in southern Europe near Spain
Both were conquered by Spanish forces in the 1500s
correctAnswer: Both were conquered by Spanish forces in the 1500s
explanation: The Aztec Empire in Mexico fell to Spanish forces and their allies in 1521, and the Inca Empire in the Andes was conquered beginning in 1532. Only the Aztec capital was on a lake, and only the Inca were in the Andes.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: A Spanish soldier and an Aztec poet each wrote about the fall of Tenochtitlan in 1521. Why would their accounts probably be different?
choices: Only one of them could really have been there at the time
Each saw the events from a different point of view
People in the 1500s had no way to write down what they saw
The city did not really fall
correctAnswer: Each saw the events from a different point of view
explanation: People on different sides of an event experience it differently. A source reflects the point of view of the person who made it, so historians compare accounts.

subject: WORLD_HISTORY
prompt: Foods such as potatoes and corn (maize) were carried from the Americas to Europe, Africa and Asia. What was one long-term result?
choices: More food could be grown, and populations rose in many places
People in Europe, Africa and Asia stopped farming their own land
Trade between the continents ended completely within a few years
correctAnswer: More food could be grown, and populations rose in many places
explanation: Potatoes and maize produce a lot of food and grow in many climates. They became important crops around the world and helped populations grow.
